title: Evaluate 30 Hz dual-camera capture
goal: Prepare a bounded 30 Hz dual-ZED UVC camera configuration matched to the 30 Hz Release control/data cadence, then provide an operator test boundary.
doneWhen: Both Release camera descriptors explicitly request 30 FPS.
Focused no-hardware checks prove the configured frame rate reaches the UVC backend configuration path.
Operator documentation states the USB/CPU stability and frame-freshness validation required before accepting 30 Hz camera data.
decisions: The data contract should request a new image for each 30 Hz control/data sample; leaving the cameras at the inherited 15 FPS would produce repeated adjacent frames.
Do not change camera resolution, image preprocessing, robot control, or safety parameters in this rate-only experiment.
The operator must validate both UVC cameras on direct USB 3.0 paths, frame freshness, and stable 30 Hz collection before using the resulting data.

verification.summary: Release commit 2315f25 requests 30 FPS from both UVC cameras and rejects a camera that reports a materially different rate. A 79-action operator trajectory had 80 unique adjacent camera frames from both views.
checks: Hydra YAML parse confirmed camera_fps=30, step_frequency=30.0, and data_collection.fps=30
Operator trajectory: both camera views had 80/80 frames and 79/79 adjacent frame changes
limitations: The collected pickle does not retain camera hardware timestamps, so achieved FPS has not been numerically measured from source timestamps.
